channel.title: Pixelburg Post
channel.description: Fictional sample stories for offline demos and tests. Not real news: the outlet, the events and the quotes are invented; the places are real so the map can show them.

item.title: Lisbon opens a new riverside tram line
item.description: Lisbon has opened a new tram line along the Tagus river. The city says the 9 kilometre route will carry 40,000 passengers a day and cut car traffic in the old town. “This line will change how people move around the old town,” the mayor said. It is the first new tram route in the city for more than 20 years. Trams will run every six minutes at peak times.

item.title: Kenya switches on its largest solar farm near Nairobi
item.description: A solar farm north of Nairobi has started supplying power to the national grid. Officials say it can light around 300,000 homes and is the biggest in East Africa so far. Its panels cover an area the size of about 400 football pitches. Engineers say the farm will feed the grid even during the dry season, when hydropower falls. A second phase is planned for next year.

item.title: Iceland volcano erupts again on the Reykjanes peninsula
item.description: A fissure eruption has started again on the Reykjanes peninsula in Iceland. Scientists say lava is flowing away from nearby towns and flights are not affected. It is the latest in a series of eruptions in the area since 2021. The fissure is about 3 kilometres long, according to the meteorological office. A nearby spa has closed as a precaution.

item.title: Heavy rain floods streets in coastal towns of Kerala
item.description: Heavy monsoon rain has flooded streets in several coastal towns in Kerala, India. Local authorities have opened 120 relief camps and closed schools for two days. Forecasters expect more heavy rain over the next three days.

item.title: Peru archaeologists uncover a 3,000-year-old temple in the Andes
item.description: Archaeologists in Peru say they have found the remains of a temple about 3,000 years old in the northern Andes. The team found painted walls and a ceremonial stairway. Excavation will continue until the rainy season begins.

item.title: Japan's bullet trains mark a record year for punctuality
item.description: Rail operators in Japan say their bullet trains ran with an average delay of under one minute last year, a record. More than 160 million passengers used the network. The fastest trains on the line reach 320 kilometres an hour. Operators credit new signalling and longer maintenance windows at night. The network carries passengers between Tokyo and Osaka in about two and a half hours.

item.title: Paris unveils plans to plant 170,000 trees by 2030
item.description: The city of Paris has announced plans to plant 170,000 trees by 2030 to cool the city in summer. Squares near the Seine will be the first to change. The city says shade can make streets several degrees cooler on the hottest days.

item.title: Storm forces ferry cancellations across the Greek islands
item.description: Strong winds have forced ferry operators to cancel sailings between Athens and several Greek islands. Coast guard officials expect services to resume on Friday. Passengers waiting at the port of Piraeus were offered places on later sailings. Gusts reached gale force in the Aegean overnight. Port authorities say no vessels have been damaged.

item.title: Brazil reports a sharp fall in Amazon deforestation
item.description: Brazil's space agency says deforestation in the Amazon fell by 30 percent over the past twelve months. Satellite images show the lowest level of clearing in a decade. Officials credit more inspections and fines for illegal clearing. Environmental groups welcomed the figures but say clearing is still rising in some states. The agency publishes its estimates every year.

item.title: Wellington schools trial a four-day week
item.description: Ten schools in Wellington, New Zealand, will trial a four-day week for one term. Education officials say they want to measure the effect on attendance and wellbeing.

item.title: Canada and Mexico sign an agreement on clean water projects
item.description: Canada and Mexico have signed an agreement to fund clean water projects in rural communities. The two governments will share the cost of 50 new treatment plants.

item.title: Moderate earthquake shakes northern Chile, no damage reported
item.description: A magnitude 5.8 earthquake shook northern Chile on Tuesday morning. Emergency services say there are no reports of damage or injuries. The quake was felt in the port city of Antofagasta. Chile sits on one of the most active seismic zones in the world.

item.title: Cairo museum opens an exhibition of ancient wooden boats
item.description: A museum in Cairo has opened a new wing to show two ancient wooden boats. Curators say the larger boat is 43 metres long and was rebuilt from 1,200 pieces. Restorers spent eight years reassembling the larger vessel. The exhibition also shows tools, ropes and paintings found with the boats. The museum expects the wing to draw thousands of visitors a day.

item.title: Seoul festival lights up the Han river with 1,000 drones
item.description: A festival in Seoul lit up the sky over the Han river with a show of 1,000 drones designed by local artists. Organisers said about 200,000 people watched from the riverbanks. The drones formed the shape of a whale above the water.

item.title: Climate talks in Nairobi – live
item.description: Follow the latest from the climate talks in Nairobi, where ministers from 40 countries are meeting this week.

item.title: Hurricane Elena makes landfall on Mexico’s Yucatán coast
item.description: Hurricane Elena has made landfall near Cancún with winds of 180 kilometres per hour. Mexico’s civil protection agency says about 1.2 million homes are without power and 40,000 people have gone to shelters. “This is a life-threatening situation,” the agency said.

item.title: Marseille wildfire: thousands evacuate from hill villages
item.description: A wildfire north of Marseille has forced about 3,000 people to leave three hill villages, officials say. Firefighters say strong winds are making the fire hard to contain. Evacuated families are staying in schools and sports halls in nearby towns.

item.title: Germany rail strike leaves stations empty
item.description: Stations across Germany were almost empty on Thursday as rail workers began a 24-hour strike over pay. The operator says only one in five long-distance trains is running. Freight trains were also affected, the operator says.

item.title: Dublin hospitals under pressure as flu cases rise
item.description: Hospitals in Dublin say their emergency departments are under severe pressure after a rise in flu cases. Health officials say 600 patients were waiting for a bed on Monday, the highest figure this year. Some planned operations have been postponed to free up beds.

item.title: Turin car plant closure threatens 2,400 jobs
item.description: A carmaker has confirmed it will close its plant near Turin by the end of next year. Unions say 2,400 jobs are at risk and have called a strike for Friday. Regional officials say they will meet the company next week.
